title: The merge tool refuses a reason flag that holds a GitHub closing keyword before a PR number
why: Text that a reason flag puts in the merge commit can close an unmerged PR on GitHub.
note: Coordinator, 03:48 CST Nov 9. Incident: at 03:37 CST batch 67's --base-red-ok reason "Fix #2390" made GitHub close #2390 unmerged; runner 8 reopened it at 03:58 CST. Fix: merge/merge.py refuses --base-red-ok, and any other flag whose text lands in the merge commit, when it holds close, closes, closed, fix, fixes, fixed, resolve, resolves or resolved before #N. The coordinator starts it. Lane session_013NEJL3115C7kVTQidSxvGj (coordinator 03:49 CST Nov 9). Notes (coordinator, 05:18 CST Nov 9, on #2412): (1) the regex backtracks quadratically on a long run of whitespace after a keyword (20k spaces take 15 s; fix `\s*(?::\s*)?`); (2) `fixes GH-2390` passes, a form GitHub's docs do not list; (3) the tests never assert the flag name in the refusal; (4) no allowed control case such as `fixtures/x#12`, and the test keeps its own copy of CLOSE_FORM instead of importing merge.CLOSE_FORM. The lane fixes (1) and (4) in a follow-up PR after #2412 merges. #2412 merged in batch 70 (PR #2498, 0e6509a96, 00:52 CST Nov 10); the follow-up PR for notes (1) and (4) can start. Part (coordinator's Explore agent (Sonnet) read of origin/main 0e6509a96, 05:01 CST Nov 10): the refusal is on main via #2412. Notes 1 and 4 are not done: the regex is still `\s*:?\s*`, and test_merge.py keeps its own CLOSE_FORM copy. Ready for that follow-up.
